title: In a Cohen-Macaulay local ring, elements cutting the dimension by their number form a regular sequence
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) whose Krull dimension $d=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is finite, and assume that $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak m$ contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $d$. Let $c\ge0$ be an integer and $g_1,\dots,g_c\in\mathfrak m$ elements such that the ring $R/(g_1,\dots,g_c)$ has Krull dimension $\dim R/(g_1,\dots,g_c)=d-c$. Then $g_1,\dots,g_c$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), first assertion, for the module M = R (the support of R/(g_1,...,g_c) is V(g_1,...,g_c), of dimension dim R/(g_1,...,g_c)); Cohen-Macaulay as in Definition Tag 00N3 (definition-CM, line 24960: dim Supp(M) = depth(M)), here depth(R) >= dim R, equivalent since the depth never exceeds the dimension
